pages.text: "Hey, move! Slowpoke!" Lolo in yellow boots pushed Riri and snatched a basket. Two shells rolled from her hands. Lots of shells were spread out to dry in the autumn yard.

"Dad will be surprised if we spread them all out!" Riri counted shells as she filled the basket. "One at a time will take forever! You are so frustrating!" Lolo snapped again. Riri shut her mouth tightly.
"Why did you put them like this? What a crooked mess!" Lolo's words grew sharper. Riri put down the basket and left the yard. Lolo was alone in the wide space. "Oh? Why did she leave?"
Mom came out in her blue apron. "Lolo, Riri's face and yours look alike, right?" Lolo nodded. "Yes, we are twins."
Mom called Riri. "Riri, could you repeat those words exactly?" Riri stood before Lolo and said, "Hey, move! Slowpoke!" Lolo's heart sank.
"A face like mine saying that to me... feels really upsetting," Lolo said softly. Mom smiled. "Words come back just like your faces." Lolo looked up. "Oh, kind words come back kindly!"
Lolo held Riri's hand. "Riri, I am sorry. The shells you chose are so smooth and shiny!" Riri held up a shell. "Really? Thank you!" Kind words come back kindly!
They sat side by side again, spreading shells. "This goes here!" "Yes, good!" Baskets hung in rows on the yard hooks. Lolo splashed yellow boots in the puddle beside the water tub and laughed.

Now Lolo knew how to speak. One, think before speaking! Two, change sharp words into kind ones! Three, say thank you and sorry first! That evening, when Riri shared half her bread, Lolo said at once, "Wow, thank you!"
Mom kissed Lolo's cheek and hugged their shoulders. Kind words came back just as kindly. Turning to Riri, Lolo said, "Kind words come back kindly!"
